title: Training in Multi-Modality Molecular and Transitional Cardiovascular Imaging
text:
Cardiovascular disease remains the major cause of morbidity in the US with the cost of care
exceeding $555 billion and as such, there has been a shift in emphasis from treatment of
disease to the prevention of disease. Prevention of cardiovascular disease necessitates early
detection and risk stratification, which may be facilitated by molecular and other multimodality
imaging approaches allowing for a more precise and personalized approach to the evaluation
and management of cardiovascular disease. For molecular imaging to emerge as a routine part
of clinical practice, appropriate education within the cardiovascular physician community and
training of a new breed of physicians and scientists is needed.

title: TRAINING GRANT IN MOLECUCLAR IMAGING RESEARCH AND CANCER SYSTEMS ANALYSIS
text:
Bringing together the tools of imaging, artificial intelligence (AI) based image analysis, computer sciences,
cellular analyses, cancer biology, and immunology will be necessary to solve current problems in oncology and
find innovative solutions that can expand the number of cancer patients who will benefit from conventional,
targeted and immunotherapies. This innovative cancer training program will prepare the next generation of
leaders in molecular imaging and cancer systems analysis science with a combination of mentored research,
coursework in a collaborative environment that has a proven record of integrating multiple disciplines to
translate science to clinical practice.

title: Assessing Everyday Function In Older Adults With The Virtual Kitchen
text:
As the U.S. population of adults over age 65 increases and as new treatments for Alzheimer’s disease and
Alzheimer’s disease related dementias (AD/ADRD) become available, there is an increasing need to efficiently
and comprehensively assess everday functional abilities to identify older adults at risk for functional disability.
This proposal evaluates the predictive and construct validity of the Virtual Kitchen Challenge- Version 2 (VKC-
2), a portable, non-immersive, virtual reality test developed for the efficient measurement of everyday function
and tests a new, comprehensive conceptual framework for understanding everyday function using the VKC-2
along with new digital approaches (e.g., smartphone digital phenotyping and EMA). Results will offer functional
assessment solutions for multiple uses and contexts, including screening older adults at risk for decline in
meaningful, functional activities in primary care, identifying cognitive and/or psychosocial targets to improve
functional abilities and promote aging in place in older adults with cognitive complaints, and as a function
endpoint in clinical trials of AD/ADRD treatments.

title: Impact of in utero metformin exposure on offspring growth and metabolic outcomes
text:
Metformin is an effective anti-diabetic agent that is increasingly prescribed to pregnant women for the
treatment of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). However, metformin, unlike insulin, readily crosses
the placenta and concerns regarding the potential impact on fetal development have not been
adequately addressed. The purpose of this study is to conduct a randomized controlled trial of insulin
versus metformin for treatment of GDM and to investigate the impact on infant growth, cellular and
placental metabolism.

title: Phenotyping and Validating Central Sensitization in Painful and Non-Painful Benign Urologic Disease Using Machine Learning
text:
RELEVANCE STATEMENT
Painful urinary conditions such as overactive bladder and interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome affect
millions of Americans and often resist treatment. This project will use existing NIH-funded data to identify how a
reactive central nervous system may give rise to pain sensitivity and explain why symptoms persist and which
treatments work best for different patients. The project will also train undergraduate students in biomedical pain
research, fostering the next generation of scientists addressing non-opioid assessment and treatment
approaches to chronic pain.

title: Studying normal and disease processes in brain with extracellular vesicles
text:
/// PROJECT NARRATIVE \\\
The molecular study of psychiatric and substance use disorders remains challenging due to the lack of direct
access to the diseased tissue in living patients. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) contain a rich repertoire of
biomolecules derived from their cell of origin and can be isolated from peripheral fluids such as blood. The
main goal of this project is to better understand what can be learned about normal and disease processes
occurring in the brain by studying brain EVs isolated from peripheral blood, and derive novel biomarkers for
schizophrenia.

title: Massachusetts NARMS Cooperative Agreement Program to Strengthen Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance in Retail Food Specimens
text:
MASPHL participation in the NARMS Cooperative Agreement Program to Strengthen Antibiotic
Resistance Surveillance in Retail Food Specimens project will enhance and strengthen
antibiotic resistance surveillance in raw retail meat and seafood.
Food samples purchased at Massachusetts retailers, screened for pathogens of interest and
characterized via subsequent laboratory testing data will not only support the goal of monitoring
antimicrobial resistance among enteric bacteria but also promote and protect public health by
contributing to the understanding of the burden of antibiotic-resistant pathogens in our nation's
food supply.

title: The role of GRK3-HDAC2 epigenetic pathway in neuroendocrine prostate cancer and immune evasion
text:
The role of GRK3-HDAC2 epigenetic pathway in neuroendocrine prostate cancer and immune evasion
Projective Narrative (Relevance)
Although potent androgen-deprivation therapies initially control prostate cancer, they increasingly drive the
development of aggressive neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), which is poorly understood and untreatable.
We have identified a new GRK3–HDAC2 epigenetic pathway that controls key features of NEPC, including
neuroendocrine differentiation, angiogenesis, and immune evasion, and this project will define its regulatory
mechanisms. Results from these studies will greatly expand our understanding of advanced prostate cancer
biology and may uncover new molecular targets for preventing and treating lethal disease.

title: Molecular and Cellular Regulation of Uterine Morphogenesis
text:
The long-term goal of my studies is to understand uterine morphogenesis, an important process for forming a
uterus capable of carrying a pregnancy to term. My proposed experiments will identify molecular and cellular
mechanisms that regulate mammalian uterine formation and will help shed light into the causes of gynecological
disorders and diseases.

title: Project 1
text: Project Summary - Project 1 The objective of this project is to generate an integrated, systems-level dataset that will enable development of models that predict disease severity or long-term sequelae in individuals infected with Lassa virus, Ebola virus or SARS-CoV-2, and protective responses to vaccines. The central hypothesis of Project 1 is that multiple variables, including individual physiological, metabolic and immunological factors, inﬂuence survival or development of long-term sequelae after infection by pathogenic RNA viruses. Additionally, we seek to determine whether or not responses to vaccines will be protective. To test this hypothesis, we have assembled unique West African and United States cohorts of individuals who are at risk for Lassa, Ebola and COVID-19 or who have survived these illnesses. Clinical trials of Lassa vaccines have recently been initiated at our clinical sites in West Africa, and we are also studying the durability of Ebola vaccines and the potential of vaccination to prevent viral reactivation in Ebola survivors. The proposed project brings together a strategically organized set of cutting edge systems tools to capture the overall immunome, antibody-ome, and metabolome of Ebola, Lassa, and COVID-19 survivors. We will use machine learning to identify unique signatures of persistent infection/disease, providing a path to diagnose, treat, and manage persistent disease following viral infection. In Aim 1, we will deﬁne physiological and metabolic attributes that distinguish Lassa, Ebola and COVID-19 survivors, non-survivors, and individuals that develop post-infection sequelae by compiling and analyzing clinical, immunological and nontraditional data, including data from wearables. In Aim 2, we will utilize high-throughput technologies, including PhIP-Seq, VirScan, and Systems Serology, to derive deep datasets to identify attributes of the humoral immune responses of Lassa, Ebola and COVID-19 patients, survivors, and vaccinees that lead to diﬀerent outcomes. In Aim 3, we will characterize anti-coronavirus immune responses in West Africans and compare the results to United States cohorts, with the goal of identifying and characterizing potentially protective responses to SARS-CoV-2. Finally, in Aim 4 we will integrate heterogeneous data types to investigate the importance of host and virus factors in determining responses to vaccines and outcome of infection with diﬀerent variants of our three viruses of interest. We will work with the Modeling Core to integrate these heterogenous data types using a combination of advanced modeling, machine learning tools, and related technologies to identify predictive biosignatures that inform: personalized treatment across sex, age, and racial diﬀerences; management strategies in acutely infected individuals and those with long term viral syndromes such as PASC; and potential targets for advanced therapeutics and improved vaccines.

title: Regulation of Soluble Adenylate Cyclase During Mammalian Sperm Capacitation
text:
Approximately one-fifth of the world's couples encounter fertility problems, half of them being attributed to the
male part. The main cause of this problem is attributed to an insufficient knowledge in sperm physiology at the
molecular level. This project will use a cross-disciplinary approach to dissect the regulation of soluble
adenylate cyclase in mammalian sperm with the goal of understanding unsolved physiological questions
related to the acquisition of sperm fertilizing competence.

title: UCSF-Bay Area Center for AIDS Research
text:
(Overall)

The restructured UCSF-Bay Area CFAR is dedicated to promoting multidisciplinary research addressing cutting-edge questions in HIV/AIDS biology, treatment, and prevention. This approach from UCSF has led to breakthrough discoveries advancing patient care and providing new approaches to curbing the HIV pandemic both locally and internationally. CFAR is also committed to supporting the next generation of HIV researchers who are critical for ending the HIV epidemic in America.

title: Cortical-hypothalamic control of the cardiovascular consequences of stress
text:
Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death globally and chronic stress is a well-known risk factor
for cardiovascular pathologies. Additionally, women have increased risk of stress-related cardiovascular
disease; however, the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this increased risk are not well understood.
Therefore, this proposal seeks to determine neural circuit-specific adaptations induced by stress that lead to
differential cardiovascular susceptibility in males and females.

title: Genetics Core for Mucin Degrading Bacteria
text: CORE B: Genetics Core for Mucin Degrading Bacteria The intestinal microbiota comprises diverse bacteria, a subset of which are capable of degrading the host-derived mucins that are a primary component of the intestinal mucus layer. Excessive erosion of the mucus layer is linked to poor health outcomes in many contexts, including patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplant, where it is associated with the development of neutropenic fever. As an essential component of the P01, we will develop a Genetics Core for Mucin Degrading Bacteria. The Core will support the three related projects in investigating the mechanisms and regulation of mucin degradation by the prevalent mucin degraders Akkermansia and Bacteroides spp. Our lab has specialized expertise in the genetic manipulation of these strictly anaerobic bacteria and contributed to developing the first set of genetic tools for Akkermansia. The primary functions of the Core will be to: (1) generate mutants in bacterial isolates and apply high-throughput genetic screens, (2) provide mutants in specific genes of interest and engineer strains for recombinant protein expression, (3) provide analysis of mucin degradation using fluorescently labelled glycans as well as human colonic mucin reagent, and (4) support bioinformatic analysis of metagenomic sequencing data, including strain identification and comparative genomics, as well as provide access to external glycan expertise. We will combine the results from the individual projects to develop a database of mucin degrading enzymes that will serve as a resource to the research community. By providing strains and reagents to gain a mechanistic understanding of bacterial mucin degradation, the proposed Core will be integral to the three proposed projects

title: Epigenetics-Based Autism Treatment with Animal Models and Human Stem Cells
text:
This study is to test the hypothesis that targeting histone demethylase LSD1 to adjust gene expression and
ameliorate synaptic defects is a novel treatment strategy for autism. Both Shank3-deficient mouse models of
autism and human neurons differentiated from stem cells of autism patient with Shank3 haploinsufficiency will
be used to test this hypothesis. This study will provide great promise for the discovery of novel
pharmacological agents to treat social deficits and repetitive behaviors associated with autism.

title: Defining molecular contributions of LINE-1 retrotransposons to AD / ADRD
text:
Project Narrative. Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRDs) are crippling
neurodegenerative disorders whose onset strongly correlates with aging. There are compelling reasons to
believe cellular senescence (effectively, cell aging) and retrotransposons (selfish DNA) may drive or
exacerbate AD and ADRDs by inducing a state of chronic stress (inflammation); more research is needed. We
will analyze the role of LINE-1 retrotransposons in senescent cells and Alzheimer's / ADRD afflicted brain
tissues, gathering additional evidence to support or refute the hypothesis that LINE-1 is a causal agent in
Alzheimer's / ADRD.

title: Environmental toxicant 1,4-dioxane drives carcinogenesis through Nrf2-dependent extracellular vesicle biogenesis
text:
Environmental pollution of 1,4-dioxane is an emerging issue in public health. The goal of this
application is to reduce the public health burden posed by environmental 1,4-dioxane exposure
through integrating new knowledges into intervention for human cancers and other health issues.
This research plan is visionary, high-risk and high-reward by focusing on the fundamental role of
the oncogenic transcription factor Nrf2 in mediating the carcinogenicity of 1,4-dioxane.

title: Ascending adrenergic control of reproductive neuroendocrine circuits
text:
Stress is increasingly associated with reproductive and sexual disorders which contribute to infertility and
conception issues in men and women. Norepinephrine-expressing brainstem neurons in the nucleus of the
solitary tract, with projections to hypothalamic regions, play a critical role in the regulation of LH secretion in
response to changes in internal state. Understanding the functional and structural organization of central
hindbrain norepinephrine circuits will provide fundamental insights into not only stress-induced infertility but major
reproductive life transitions, such as puberty and aging across sexes.

title: The International Workshop on Molecular Aspects of Myeloid Stem Cell Development and Leukemia
text:
The International Workshop on Molecular Aspects of Myeloid Stem Cell Development and Leukemia is the
premier global meeting which spans fundamental stem cell biology and function, myeloid cell differentiation,
marrow failure syndromes and myeloid cell malignancies. Scientists with expertise in normal and abnormal
hematopoiesis and clinicians who treat patients with myeloid leukemias, malignancies, and pre-leukemic
disorders and also have active research programs in these diseases achieve a better understanding of critical
steps/factors that regulate hematopoiesis, their impact on leukemogenesis, and their potential relevance in
clinical settings.

title: Therapeutic Targeting of Upregulated BAP1 in Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma
text:
Primary liver cancer is a serious and often deadly type of tumor with few effective treatments. In this study, we
will focus on a gene called BAP1, which is found at high levels in liver cancer. We aim to understand how BAP1
contributes to the development of liver cancer and explore ways to target it as a potential treatment against liver
cancer.
